title: Brief meeting
rule: Played as romance: glances through the glass, a lingering thanks, the lost errand as a heart's distraction.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

made: seven collage panels (the third an oval vignette across the page) glued on the LoC sheet, under a masthead slip 'BRIEF MEETING' with two rose-paper hearts

page 12's Daumier collage kit reused: the bourgeois of 'Il est devenu pro-pri-e-taire !' (1846) as the AGENT; the bonneted woman and the carriage window of 'Un premier voyage en chemin de fer' (1846) as the STRANGER and the TICKET OFFICE window; the CONCIERGE door as the SERVICE door; desk, counter, cupboard and clock case cut from the prints' own crayon tone (incl. the tunnel black of 'L'entree du grand tunnel', 1843); the ANRC 1922 key in the cupboard
the oval close-up: her head and shoulders cut from her figure at 1.85x, his figure at 1.3x, the pane cut from the carriage window's pale paper with tunnel-black sash bars and white pen glints

HANDMADE: rose-paper hearts (heart curve cut as scissor facets, rim and shadow), romance narration slips, pen-hand balloons with the four canon lines verbatim, pencil to his chin, hand-ruled borders and the oval's pen line

events.E0: P1: desk, memo slip ('4:15 - open SERVICE door. Key in cupboard.'), he has risen; 'Nothing else on his mind'
events.E1: P2: she at the TICKET OFFICE window; question balloon; 'a voice at the glass'; P3: the glance through the pane
events.E2: P4: clock at 4:10, he looks up; answer balloon
events.E3: P5: thanks balloon, she turns away; 'Her thanks lingered... and then she was gone'
events.E4: P6: the cupboard open, the key on its hook tagged SERVICE
events.E5: P7: pencil to chin, forgetting balloon, a heart drifting where the errand was; key on its hook; SERVICE door shut

beat: the glance: in the oval panel the two cut-out faces slide toward each other across the pane and the rose heart is glued between them; then the thanks raises its little hearts; then the forgetting balloon and the drifting heart
beat_frames: b01: panels 1-3, the faces apart, no heart
b03: faces at the pane, heart glued on
b04: + panels 4-5, the thanks without hearts
b05: the hearts rise from the thanks
b06: + panels 6-7, no forgetting line, no heart
b07: forgetting balloon and drifting heart (= the page)

self_check.genre_signals: masthead 'BRIEF MEETING / a love story at the ticket window'; an oval close-up of the two faces with the pane between them and a rose-paper heart; romance narration ('Their eyes met through the pane', 'He would have given her the clock', 'Her thanks lingered', 'his heart was out on the platform; the errand had gone with her'); hearts rising from the thanks and one drifting above his head at the forgetting
self_check.outcome: key on its hook, SERVICE door closed (caption and picture)
self_check.pending: independent blind reading not run by the maker
